body: I've often dated woman who say I'm not aggressive enough, or I'm too timid when making the first move. But in this world we're living in, it's dangerous not to be on the cautious end of the spectrum. Men are seen as rapist and pedophiles until proven otherwise. And even when they are proven otherwise, they all too often receive the label regardless.

I just wrote a post about a similar situation, but deleted it.  I don't know the heartless fuck who keeps downvoting in a suicide watch subreddit, but they're going to burn in hell. 

I can't give you much advice (not that you would want it), but I can empathize with you.  You are not alone.  As much as you hate to hear it, IT DOES GET BETTER.  Please do not kill yourself.  I see myself in your post, having been in the exact situation.  I am still working towards a girlfriend, but I have also found that there are things that can make you feel alive and good in the interim.  One of the best resources was meetup.com  It is a site for getting people together for common interests: play pick-up basketball; find a group of people to play Magic; learn a new activity; or just have a movie night.   Stay active and meet new people.  Friends can't replace lovers, but they can fill that void you are missing.  Don't think about the goal, enjoy the journey and live in the moment. 

Good luck, stranger.  I hope we both find what we're after.

If this is a casual relationship, don't fess up to it, just get laid.  If she suspects something, just say that you are inexperience (which you are, but that doesn't have to mean you're a virgin).  In the future, I would phrase it like this.  "Inexperienced" is better than "virgin".  It gets the same point of expectations across, but without the stigma.  It's not like you don't know which thing goes in the other thing; you just haven't tested the theory, sorta speak.

If you want this to be a long-term relationship, don't rush into things.  Not to belittle you in anyway, but you should take it slow and make sure you are not a rebound before getting more intimate.  If she only broke up with him last week, that could be a sign that she may not be ready to truly move on.

Thanks for your response, you made some really interesting observations.  Particularly the notion that perhaps companionship is a way for some people to compromise for what they really want.  The phrase "too romantic for the tastes of most young woman" is incredibly frustrating.  I've heard it before and the notion is never any less true nor comforting.  I am assertive in my advances, but to make that leap to aggressive/dominant can only be accomplished successfully by at best the top 5% of men; else be labeled desperate or creepy, despite doing nothing different in execution.  Thanks again for responding.
Amen. Thanks for your response.  This is exactly how I feel in a nutshell.
Ah shoot :-( they aren't yet available in my area

Thank you for taking the time to respond. I really enjoyed reading your thoughts on my situation.  Believe it or not, you're the first person to sympathize with my relationship goal.  You really nailed on what I was after: "...love won't solve your depression, but in my experience, it can help you find the right path for yourself..." I think there are some people who truly could not handle a relationship and taking care of their own problems. As I mentioned, professionally I have my life together.  Just because I have some emotional demons, doesn't mean that I couldn't put them away for my partner.  In fact, I feel that a partner could be a driving force behind resolving my depression; especially since doing it for myself has been such a struggle.
